faq.title: FAQ
faq.subtitle: Short answers about the program and the site

items.question: What is a lost score?
answer: Until October 2024 the osu!stable server kept one play per beatmap and mod combination: the one with the highest score. A new play with a higher score replaced the old one even when the old play was worth more pp, and a play that scored less than your record was not kept at all.
That pp disappeared from your profile. Your local replays still have those plays, and Lost Scores reads them back.

items.question: Is it safe for my account?
answer: The program does not touch the game. It reads the replays and beatmaps in your osu! folder and asks the official osu! API about maps and your profile. It never changes files and never sends scores to osu!.

items.question: Why log in with osu!?
answer: Logged in, the program asks the Lost Scores server instead of osu!. The server shares one map cache and one queue to osu! between all players, so you need no keys of your own. It also saves your scans to your profile and lets you publish them.
You log in on osu!'s own page, so the program never sees your password. You can use the keys of your own osu! OAuth application instead.

items.question: Who sees my scans?
answer: Logged in, every scan is saved to your profile, where only you see it; the 20 newest are kept. Share in the program publishes a scan: then everyone sees it on your profile and in the <hall>Hall of Copium</hall>. Replays are shared only if you tick the replay box on the Share card. You can unpublish or delete a scan at any time.

items.question: What does verified mean?
answer: Every published scan is checked against osu! within a few minutes. The check compares your profile pp, rank and accuracy, your online top and how the Potential Top adds up.

Then it takes the ten lost plays that matter most for your place: the five highest and five more picked at random, with bigger plays more likely. For each one it checks the map and its status, that the play was set after the map was ranked and before 9 October 2024, that osu! has a play with the same mods and a higher score that replaced it, and that the lost play is not on osu! anymore. A scan that passes is verified. Until then it shows checking.

items.question: How is the Hall of Copium counted?
answer: Players are ordered by how much pp their profile would gain if their lost plays counted: the Potential Top total minus the profile pp osu! shows. Each player appears once, with the newest published scan.

The Plays tab ranks single plays instead, by the pp lost on one map: what the lost play was worth minus the play osu! kept with the same mods. The two numbers differ. A play that lost 80 pp on its map adds less to the profile, because the profile weights every play by its place in the top.

items.question: How do I watch a replay?
answer: If a player shared replays, their lost plays have a replay button on the profile and in the Plays tab. It downloads an .osr file. Open it with osu!stable, by double-clicking it or dragging it onto the game window, and the game plays it back. osu! needs the same version of the map the play was set on.

items.question: Does it work with lazer or other modes?
answer: No. It reads osu!stable replays from the osu! folder, and only osu!standard plays.

items.question: Why does Windows or macOS warn me?
answer: The builds are not signed with a paid certificate yet, so the system does not know the publisher. <download>Download</download> shows how to open the program the first time.

items.question: How do I delete my data?
answer: The trash button next to Share deletes a scan from the server. To remove everything the server keeps about your account, write to <mail/>. The <privacy>privacy page</privacy> lists what is kept.

items.question: Where do I report a bug?
answer: Open an issue on <issues>GitHub</issues> or write to <mail/>.

sections.title: Who runs Lost Scores
text: osu! Lost Scores is a fan project by KZ_Lemon4ik. It consists of the desktop program, this website at lost.lemon4ik.kz and the server behind both. It is not made or endorsed by ppy Pty Ltd, and osu! is a trademark of ppy Pty Ltd.
For questions about this policy or about your data, write to <mail/>.

sections.title: The program on your computer
text: The program reads the replays and beatmaps in your osu! folder and does not change them. It has no telemetry and sends nothing about your computer. Unless you log in with osu!, scan results stay on your computer.

To scan, the program asks for public information about your osu! profile, your online top and the beatmaps that may hold a lost play, identified by beatmap ids and MD5 hashes. With the osu! login these requests go through our server, which asks osu! on your behalf; with your own osu! API keys they go to osu! directly. The program also loads avatars and beatmap covers from osu!, asks GitHub once a day whether a new version exists, or our mirror if GitHub cannot be reached, and uploads pictures to catbox.moe only when you press that button.

sections.title: Data we keep
text: When you log in with osu!, we receive and keep your osu! user id, your username and your earlier usernames, and the times your account was first and last seen. We do not receive your password or your email address.

While you are logged in, every finished scan is saved on our server: the lost plays, the Potential Top and the summary figures. Replay files are uploaded only for the plays you choose to share. We also keep the results of the checks of published scans, a daily count of requests per account that keeps the shared queue fair, and map information shared by all players.
The server does not store IP addresses or browser details.

sections.title: How the data is used
text: The data is used only to provide what you ask for: to find the maps of your scan, to keep your scans in your profile, to show the scans you publish and to check them against osu!. We do not sell data, show advertising or use your data for marketing.

sections.title: Who can see your scans
text: Saved scans are private. Only you can see them, after logging in on this website or in the program.

When you publish a scan, anyone can see it on your profile page and in the Hall of Copium, together with your osu! username and avatar, and anyone can download the replays you shared with it. You can unpublish or delete a published scan at any time.

sections.title: How long data is kept
text: We keep your 20 newest private scans and delete older ones automatically. A published scan and its replays stay until you unpublish or delete them. A login session lasts up to 90 days and ends when you log out. Answers from osu! about your profile are cached for five minutes.

When a published scan is deleted, we keep only a note that the account had a flagged check: the account, the number of flagged checks and the time of the last one. Nothing from the scan itself remains.

sections.title: Service providers
text: The website and the server run on Cloudflare, which handles the network traffic and stores our data under its own privacy policy. The website loads avatars from osu! (a.ppy.sh), and the Download page asks GitHub for the latest version of the program.

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
text: The website sets one cookie, and only after you log in: your session, which scripts on the page cannot read. Your choice of theme, language and animations is stored in your browser's local storage. There are no analytics, advertising or tracking cookies.

sections.title: Your choices
text: You can see all your scans on your profile, publish, unpublish or delete them, and log out at any time. To delete your account and everything kept with it, or to ask what we keep about you, write to <mail/>.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
text: When this policy changes, the date at the top of the page changes as well.
